subject: Cross-border connection authorization & peering — EU/APAC failover acceptance
messages:
From: Olivia Jensen <olivia.jensen@seacloud.dk>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@seacloud.dk
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 14:17:00 +0200
Subject: Cross-border peering request and EU residency constraints

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. NordicBank is moving fast and wants to progress the private deployment conversation. Before we lock in bandwidth and capacity, Seacloud needs a formal peering/authorization plan that ensures:

- All customer data for NordicBank stays in EU primary sites (no tokens or logs leave EU tenancy).
- Failover to APAC is allowed only as an emergency warm-standby, with explicit trigger conditions and audit trail.
- Clear IP ranges, ASN, and interconnect requirements (we prefer IPsec or PrivateLink-style peering).
- A mutually agreed DR test window (we propose 2027-06-25) and rollback criteria.

I attached our peering template to make this concrete (seacloud-peering-template.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's acceptance criteria and provide a draft mutual action plan we can share with NordicBank security?

Best,
Olivia Jensen
Partnerships & Network Security
Seacloud Systems

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Jensen <olivia.jensen@seacloud.dk>

Hi Olivia — thanks for the template and the clarity. Short answer: we can support the model but we need to lock acceptance criteria and owners. Proposed next steps: 

1) Technical call between Seacloud NetOps, Priyom (arch), and Vivek (ops) — propose Mon 14 Jun 09:00 BST.
2) Redwood to provide: public ASN (to be used for BGP), allowed IP ranges, encryption mode (IPsec preferred), and DR test plan stub.
3) Legal touchpoint (Laura) for DPA addendum + KMS residency proof.

I assigned Priyom and Vivek to draft the network acceptance checklist. Laura, can you list must-have legal items we should surface? Olivia — we'll aim to return a MAP (mutual action plan) by EOD Mon.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Jensen <olivia.jensen@seacloud.dk>, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Cross-border peering request and EU residency constraints

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 09:02 Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I assigned Priyom and Vivek to draft the network acceptance checklist.

Thanks — looping in a few technical bullets from the architecture side. High-level constraints and our suggested acceptance criteria: 

- Residency model: Primary cluster in eu-west-1 (Redwood Private tenant) with asynchronous replication to apac-southeast-1 warm standby. We avoid synchronous replication across continents due to latency and consistency risk.
- Failover mode: Manual promotion only; automatic failover requires explicit cross-party approval. Acceptable emergency triggers: complete EU-region outage > 15 minutes OR documented regulatory directive.
- Connectivity: IPsec tunnels + BGP (MD5 auth), OR PrivateLink with mutually-authenticated endpoints. We will provide sample IKEv2 profiles.
- IPs/ASN: Redwood will provide a /20 aggregate for peering plus a separate /24 for health/probes. Seacloud to confirm allowed ingress filters.
- KV cache and prefix-caching: must remain within EU tenant; we will provide a config flag to disable cross-region cache replication.

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- Whitelisted IPs received and confirmed by Seacloud.
- Shared IKEv2 certs exchanged and tested.
- BGP session established and routes advertised (as expected).
- Application-level smoke tests pass (token generation, embeddings, model inference) within EU.
- DR test executed in maintenance window with documented rollback.

Attaching a rough topology (redwood-network-topology-v1.drawio). Vivek — can you add failover test steps and assign owners?

—Priyom (on behalf of Infra Architecture)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, Olivia Jensen <olivia.jensen@seacloud.dk>, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:09:00 +0530
Subject: RE: Cross-border peering request and EU residency constraints

Thanks Priyom — adding ops-level details and a proposed DR window.

Operational notes:
- BGP / routing policy: we will tag routes with a BGP community for "preferred-eu". Failover will withdraw preferred-eu and advertise "standby-apac".
- Test window: 2027-06-25 02:00-05:00 UTC (low traffic). Suggest a dry-run on 2027-06-23 where we run connectivity checks without changing active routes.
- Monitoring and audits: all route changes and elevation commands will be logged to our audit trail (immutable) and a snapshot pushed to the shared Drive folder.
- Backout: if any smoke test fails, we will revert within 30 minutes and file a postmortem.

Attachments: dr-test-plan-2027-06-25.xlsx (test steps + owner matrix).

Olivia — can Seacloud confirm an ops contact for the DR run and whether you require a runbook format (we can provide runbook + runbook checklist).

—Vivek (Infra Ops)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, Olivia Jensen <olivia.jensen@seacloud.dk>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Cross-border peering request and EU residency constraints

Quick legal checklist for the MAP:

- DPA addendum referencing: EU data residency, controller/processor roles, logging retention limits, and accepted subprocessors.
- KMS residency: Redwood must provide proof that customer keys (or wrapped keys) for NordicBank remain in EU KMS.
- Cross-border transfer gating: include an explicit customer acceptance step prior to any APAC activation.
- Audit evidence: specify the artifacts Seacloud and Redwood must produce post-DR run (route snapshots, audit logs, runbook execution notes).

I'll draft a short addendum and share via DocuSign for signatures (link to follow). We should avoid broad language that allows automatic cross-border failover without customer sign-off.

—Laura Bennett, Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
